newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Foncier inquiry agreed "in principle".
newsitem.headline: Cr Foncier inquiry agreed "in principle".

text.p: The French National Assembly's finance committee agreed in principle to set up a commission of inquiry into troubled property lender Credit Foncier, parliamentarian Jean-Jacques Guillet said on Wednesday.

Guillet told Reuters the committee voted in favour but that it would question Justice Minister Jacques Toubon on Wednesday on legal proceedings involving a Credit Foncier subsidiary before taking a definitive decision on the matter.

Guillet also said after hearings with Finance Minister Jean Arthuis and Credit Foncier boss Jerome Meyssonnier on Tuesday that there were "differences of appreciation" between the two men on the profit outlook as well as the 1995 accounts which triggered an Arthuis plan to win the group down.
A petition for the creation of a commission of inquiry was proposed by Guillet, a politician belonging to Prime Minister Alain Jupppe's Gaullist RPR party, with the support of around 100 signatories.
He and other politicians have demanded an enquiry to examine the circumstances surrounding the government's decision to take over the property lender and wind it down.
The lender posted a loss of 10.8 billion francs for 1995, including 13.6 billion francs in provisions for exposure to a property market which collapsed at the end of the 1980s.
Meysonnier's forecast that the group could post a profit of up to one billion francs this year has reinforced calls on Arthuis to re-examine its plans.
"There's a clear difference of appreciation between Arthuis and Meysonnier. Should we believe the Treasury or the chairman of Credit Foncier, who Mr Arthuis says he has full trust," guillet said.
"They do not agree on the provisions" (in the 1995 accounts), Guillet said.
Meysonnier had also told parliamentarians on Tuesday that he felt the group could keep operating without a recapitalisation while looking for an ally, Guillet added.

At the moment the group's shareholder funds are negative to the tune of more than two billion francs but it has a state guarantee securing its bond obligations. Credit Foncier is one of the country's biggest debt issuers after the state.
